h1:
Thai Cooking Classes
Which Class & Where to Book
intro: Thai cooking classes are one of the most popular activities for travelers — you visit a fresh market, learn the ingredients, cook everything yourself, then sit down and eat what you made. Most classes run half a day to a full day, are taught in English, and can be adapted for vegetarians. This guide covers where to study, what prices to expect, what dishes are on the menu, and where to book ahead.
quickAnswerHtml: Most Thai cooking classes follow the same format: market walk to pick ingredients → cook 4–6 dishes → eat what you made, plus recipes to take home. Chiang Mai is the top destination (many classes are garden-based with herb-picking), followed by Bangkok and island destinations like Phuket, Krabi, and Samui. Half-day classes run around 800–1,500 THB; full-day around 1,200–2,000 THB. Almost all are taught in English, vegetarian/vegan menus are available on request, and booking ahead is strongly recommended — popular classes fill up fast.

blocks.html: Thai cooking classes suit everyone, from total beginners to serious food lovers. The standard format is a market walk with the chef to explore ingredients, followed by cooking classic Thai dishes one by one, then sitting down to eat everything you made and taking the recipes home. Many classes offer hotel pickup and drop-off from central areas.

items: Half-day (3–4 hrs) — cook 3–4 dishes, suits anyone short on time; choose a morning or evening session
Full-day (5–6 hrs) — more in-depth market visit, cook 5–6 dishes, including making your own curry paste from scratch
Morning sessions usually include the fresh-market walk; evening sessions suit late risers
Almost every class can go vegetarian or vegan, or avoid allergens — just let them know at booking

blocks.html: The most popular dishes in Thai cooking classes include Pad Thai, Tom Yum Kung, Green Curry (with homemade paste), Pad Kra Pao, Som Tam, Tod Mun, and Mango Sticky Rice. Many classes let you pick some dishes yourself. For a lot of people the highlight is pounding fresh curry paste in a stone mortar — the flavor difference from store-bought paste is striking.

Popular classes fill up quickly, especially in high season. Booking online in advance locks in the session you want and lets you compare prices and reviews before paying. The options below bring together classes from multiple operators in one place.

faq.q: Where is the best place to take a Thai cooking class?
faq.a: Chiang Mai is the most popular — it has the widest choice of classes, many set in gardens or on farms with herb-picking. Bangkok comes second (fresh market walk in the city), followed by island destinations like Phuket, Krabi, and Samui.

faq.q: How much does a Thai cooking class cost?
faq.a: Half-day classes run around 800–1,500 THB and full-day classes around 1,200–2,000 THB, depending on the city, number of dishes, and whether hotel transfers are included. Check live prices when booking online.

faq.q: I've never cooked before — can I still join?
faq.a: Absolutely. Classes are designed for complete beginners. The chef guides you step by step in English and everyone cooks together dish by dish. No prior experience needed.

faq.q: Are there vegetarian or vegan options?
faq.a: Almost every class can be adapted to vegetarian or vegan diets, and allergens can usually be avoided too — just let them know at booking or before the class starts.

faq.q: Do I need to book in advance?
faq.a: Yes, it's strongly recommended. Popular classes fill up quickly, especially in high season. Booking online in advance secures the session you want and lets you compare prices and reviews before paying.
